guide.name: The Blue Ridge Parkway from Shenandoah to Cherokee
guide.description: Five days down all 469 miles of the parkway, from Rockfish Gap in Virginia to the Great Smoky Mountains, with overlooks, short hikes, old mills and lodges. Sections close for weather and repairs; check NPS road status.

sections.name: Day 1 · Rockfish Gap to Peaks of Otter · 86 mi
Day 2 · Peaks of Otter to Mabry Mill · 90 mi
Day 3 · Mabry Mill to Blowing Rock · 116 mi
Day 4 · Blowing Rock to Asheville · 90 mi

properties.name: Humpback Rocks
properties.notes: The first real climb south of Rockfish Gap: a short, steep trail from Humpback Gap to a bare rock summit over the Shenandoah Valley. The visitor center and pioneer farm buildings are just up the road at milepost 5.8.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 6, Lyndhurst, VA 22952

properties.name: Ravens Roost Overlook
properties.notes: A cliff-edge pullout facing west over the Shenandoah Valley and Torry Mountain. Rock climbers use the ledge; everyone else comes for the late-afternoon light.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 10.7, Lyndhurst, VA 22952

properties.name: Devils Backbone Basecamp Brewpub
properties.notes: A big timber-frame brewpub in the Rockfish Valley, down VA-664 from Reeds Gap. A good lunch or dinner stop, with a lawn out back and a campground nearby run by the same brewery.
properties.address: 200 Crandall Run, Roseland, VA 22967

properties.name: Crabtree Falls
properties.notes: A string of cascades dropping more than 1,000 feet, reached by a short detour down VA-56 from milepost 27. The lower overlook is a few minutes from the lot; the full climb to the top takes a couple of hours round trip.
properties.address: 11581 Crabtree Falls Hwy, Tyro, VA 22976

properties.name: Yankee Horse Ridge
properties.notes: A pullout with a rebuilt stretch of narrow-gauge logging railroad and a short walk to Wigwam Falls. A quick leg-stretch on the way down to the James River.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 34.4, Vesuvius, VA 24483

properties.name: Natural Bridge State Park
properties.notes: A 200-foot limestone arch over Cedar Creek, about a half-hour off the parkway near the James River crossing. The creekside trail runs under the bridge past Saltpeter Cave to Lace Falls. Worth the detour if you have a spare afternoon.
properties.address: 6477 S Lee Hwy, Natural Bridge, VA 24578

properties.name: James River Visitor Center
properties.notes: The parkway's lowest point, where it crosses the James. A footbridge under the road leads to a restored lock from the old James River and Kanawha Canal. Bridge repair work has brought detours here; check NPS road status.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 63.6, Big Island, VA 24526

properties.name: Sunset Field Overlook
properties.notes: Trailhead for Apple Orchard Falls, a 200-foot falls reached by a steep descent through a hardwood cove. Plan on a couple of hours and save energy for the climb back up.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 78.4, Buchanan, VA 24066

properties.name: Peaks of Otter Visitor Center
properties.notes: Ranger desk and exhibits at the foot of Sharp Top. From here you can walk to the restored Johnson Farm or loop around Abbott Lake.
properties.address: 85919 Blue Ridge Pkwy, Bedford, VA 24523

properties.name: Sharp Top Trail
properties.notes: A stiff climb up stone steps to the rocky summit of Sharp Top, with a full circle of views across the Piedmont and the ridges. Start early on fall weekends, when the lot fills.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 86, Bedford, VA 24523

properties.name: Peaks of Otter Lodge
properties.notes: The only lodge on the Virginia side of the parkway, set on Abbott Lake with every room facing the water and Sharp Top. The dining room is the one sit-down meal for miles. Seasonal; book well ahead for October.
properties.address: 85554 Blue Ridge Pkwy, Bedford, VA 24523

properties.name: Explore Park
properties.notes: A county park along the Roanoke River at milepost 115 with a parkway visitor center, trails, river access, and cabins, yurts and campsites for an inexpensive night near the road.
properties.address: 3900 Rutrough Rd, Vinton, VA 24014

properties.name: Mill Mountain Star
properties.notes: Roanoke's giant neon star on Mill Mountain, reached by a spur road from milepost 120. The overlook takes in the whole city; come back after dark to see it lit.
properties.address: 2404 Prospect Rd SE, Roanoke, VA 24014

properties.name: The Hotel Roanoke & Conference Center
properties.notes: The Tudor-style railroad hotel across the tracks from downtown, built in the 1880s and still the city's grand old address. A pedestrian bridge leads straight into the Market district.
properties.address: 110 Shenandoah Ave NW, Roanoke, VA 24016

properties.name: Texas Tavern
properties.notes: A ten-stool hot dog and chili counter that has been feeding downtown Roanoke since 1930. Order a cheesy western and a bowl of chili, and expect to wait for a seat.
properties.address: 114 W Church Ave, Roanoke, VA 24011

properties.name: Floyd Country Store
properties.notes: Old-time and bluegrass music hub in the town of Floyd, about six miles off the parkway on VA-8. Weekend shows pack the floor with flatfoot dancers; check the official site for the music calendar.
properties.address: 206 S Locust St, Floyd, VA 24091

properties.name: Hotel Floyd
properties.notes: A small hotel built with green materials a short walk from the Country Store, with rooms named for and furnished by local artists and craftspeople. Handy if you want to stay for a night of music.
properties.address: 300 Rick Lewis Way, Floyd, VA 24091

properties.name: Rock Castle Gorge Trail
properties.notes: A long, demanding loop that drops from the open meadows of Rocky Knob into a deep gorge and climbs back. For a shorter outing, walk only the grassy ridgetop stretch along the parkway.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 167, Floyd, VA 24091

properties.name: Chateau Morrisette
properties.notes: A winery just off milepost 171.5 in a big timber-frame building, with a restaurant and tastings. Reservations are a good idea for a meal.
properties.address: 291 Winery Rd SW, Floyd, VA 24091

properties.name: Mabry Mill
properties.notes: The gristmill on a millpond that ends up on half the parkway postcards. A short path passes a blacksmith shop and other farm buildings. The restaurant and gift shop have closed, so plan to eat elsewhere.
properties.address: 266 Mabry Mill Rd SE, Meadows of Dan, VA 24120

properties.name: Puckett Cabin
properties.notes: The log cabin of Orelena Puckett, a midwife who delivered babies across these hills into the 1930s. A two-minute stop with a good story attached.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 189.9, Meadows of Dan, VA 24120

properties.name: Blue Ridge Music Center
properties.notes: Exhibits on the fiddle and banjo traditions of the region, with local musicians often playing on the breezeway and an outdoor amphitheater for summer concerts. Check the official site for the schedule.
properties.address: 700 Foothills Rd, Galax, VA 24333

properties.name: Cumberland Knob
properties.notes: Just past the North Carolina line, the first recreation area built on the parkway. An easy loop climbs to the knob, and the Gully Creek trail drops into a ravine for something harder.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 217.5, Ennice, NC 28623

properties.name: Brinegar Cabin
properties.notes: A homestead cabin and garden at Doughton Park, where the meadows open up on both sides of the road. Good place to watch for deer at dusk.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 238.5, Laurel Springs, NC 28644

properties.name: The Bluffs Restaurant
properties.notes: A parkway coffee shop dating to 1949, with a curved counter and country cooking, reopened with help from the Blue Ridge Parkway Foundation. It is seasonal and has run on limited days, so check its site before planning lunch around it.
properties.address: 45338 Blue Ridge Pkwy, Laurel Springs, NC 28644

properties.name: E. B. Jeffress Park
properties.notes: Trailhead for the Cascades, a short loop through rhododendron to viewing platforms beside a long slide of water down a rock face. Stay behind the railings; the rock is slick.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 271.9, Deep Gap, NC 28618

properties.name: The Blowing Rock
properties.notes: The cliff that gave the town its name, where updrafts out of the Johns River Gorge can push light objects back up. Privately run since the 1930s, with a view to Grandfather Mountain.
properties.address: 432 The Rock Rd, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

properties.name: Blowing Rock Art & History Museum
properties.notes: A compact museum just off Main Street with rotating shows of Appalachian art and the town's history as a mountain resort. A good rainy-day stop.
properties.address: 159 Ginny Stevens Ln, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

match.query: Blowing Rock Art and History Museum

properties.name: The Speckled Trout
properties.notes: A long-running Main Street restaurant where mountain trout is the dish to order. Easy to walk to from most of the town's inns.
properties.address: 922 Main St, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

properties.name: Green Park Inn
properties.notes: A white clapboard hotel from the late 1800s sitting right on the Eastern Continental Divide. Old-fashioned rooms, a wide porch and the Divide Tavern, which straddles the line.
properties.address: 9239 Valley Blvd, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

properties.name: Chetola Resort
properties.notes: A lakeside resort on an old estate at the edge of town, a short walk from Main Street and a few minutes from Moses Cone. The splurge stay of the trip.
properties.address: 185 Chetola Lake Dr, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

properties.name: Moses H. Cone Memorial Park
properties.notes: Flat Top Manor, a 1901 summer house with a long porch facing Bass Lake, now holds a craft shop of the Southern Highland Craft Guild. Miles of old carriage roads wind around the estate for walking or riding.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 294, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

properties.name: Price Lake
properties.notes: A still mountain lake with Grandfather Mountain reflected in it on calm mornings. A flat trail loops all the way around the shore.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 297, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

properties.name: Julian Price Park Campground
properties.notes: The parkway's biggest campground, with lakeside tent sites and an easy walk to Price Lake. The budget way to sleep near Blowing Rock; reserve through Recreation.gov.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 297, Blowing Rock, NC 28605

properties.name: Linn Cove Viaduct
properties.notes: The S-curved concrete bridge that wraps the side of Grandfather Mountain, the last piece of the parkway finished, in 1987. The Tanawha Trail passes underneath for the classic view from below.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 304, Linville, NC 28646

properties.name: Grandfather Mountain
properties.notes: Privately run nature park with the Mile High Swinging Bridge, wildlife habitats and steep trails along the ridge. The entrance is on US-221 about a mile south of milepost 305. Wind and ice can close the mountain; check the official site.
properties.address: 2050 Blowing Rock Hwy, Linville, NC 28646

match.skip: No matching Apple Maps listing near this point (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: Linville Falls
properties.notes: The falls where the Linville River drops into Linville Gorge. The spur road and trails have reopened after Helene, but some facilities nearby, including the campground and picnic area, remain closed; check the NPS site.
properties.address: Linville Falls Spur Rd, Linville Falls, NC 28647

properties.name: Famous Louise's Rock House Restaurant
properties.notes: A 1930s stone tavern where three counties meet, serving country breakfasts, ribs and homemade pies. A short hop from the Linville Falls exit.
properties.address: 23175 Linville Falls Hwy, Linville Falls, NC 28647

properties.name: Switzerland Inn
properties.notes: A Swiss-chalet style inn in the old resort village of Little Switzerland, reached from milepost 334, with rooms looking off the edge of the ridge. South of here the parkway has had long Helene repair closures; check NPS road status for the detour.
properties.address: 86 High Ridge Rd, Little Switzerland, NC 28749

properties.name: Mount Mitchell State Park
properties.notes: The highest summit east of the Mississippi, reached by NC-128 from milepost 355. A short paved path climbs from the summit lot to an observation deck. The park closes often in winter, and the top can be much colder than the valleys.
properties.address: 2388 NC-128, Burnsville, NC 28714

properties.name: Craggy Gardens Visitor Center
properties.notes: Grassy balds covered in rhododendron. A trail from the visitor center climbs to the bald, and the Craggy Pinnacle trail starts from a lot just north for a ring of views. Some trails and the picnic area may be closed; check the NPS site.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 364.5, Barnardsville, NC 28709

properties.name: Folk Art Center
properties.notes: Home of the Southern Highland Craft Guild, with a gallery of historic Appalachian crafts and a shop selling work by guild members. Craftspeople often demonstrate in the lobby.
properties.address: 382 Blue Ridge Pkwy, Asheville, NC 28805

properties.name: The Omni Grove Park Inn
properties.notes: The granite-boulder resort from 1913 on Sunset Mountain, with fireplaces big enough to stand in and a terrace looking over the city to the Blue Ridge. Stop in for a drink at sunset even if you sleep elsewhere.
properties.address: 290 Macon Ave, Asheville, NC 28804

properties.name: Cúrate
properties.notes: Downtown Spanish tapas bar with a long counter facing the kitchen. Book ahead, or try for a seat at the bar.
properties.address: 13 Biltmore Ave, Asheville, NC 28801

properties.name: French Broad Chocolate Lounge
properties.notes: Truffles, cakes and drinking chocolate on Pack Square. The line moves faster than it looks.
properties.address: 10 S Pack Sq, Asheville, NC 28801

properties.name: Sunny Point Café
properties.notes: West Asheville's breakfast institution, with a kitchen garden out front and biscuits worth the wait. Fuel up here before the last day.
properties.address: 626 Haywood Rd, Asheville, NC 28806

properties.name: Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center
properties.notes: The parkway's main visitor center at milepost 384, with a long wall map of the whole road and rangers who know current closures. Good place to plan the final stretch.
properties.address: 195 Hemphill Knob Rd, Asheville, NC 28803

properties.name: The North Carolina Arboretum
properties.notes: Gardens, a bonsai collection and miles of trails in Bent Creek, right off milepost 393. Easy to spend a morning.
properties.address: 20 Fredrick Law Olmsted Way, Asheville, NC 28806

properties.name: Mount Pisgah Trail
properties.notes: A rocky, steepening climb of about a mile and a half from the Mount Pisgah parking area to the summit beside the broadcast tower. Views reach back toward Asheville across land George Vanderbilt once owned.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 407.6, Canton, NC 28716

properties.name: Pisgah Inn
properties.notes: A ridgetop motor inn whose rooms look east over the Pisgah forest, with a restaurant facing the same view. Open spring through fall; meals need reservations, so book early.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 408.6, Canton, NC 28716

properties.name: Looking Glass Rock Overlook
properties.notes: A pullout facing the bare granite dome of Looking Glass Rock, which shines when wet. One of the easiest big views of the day.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 417, Brevard, NC 28712

match.skip: No matching Apple Maps listing near this point (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: Graveyard Fields
properties.notes: A high valley of blueberry thickets and waterfalls, with a short walk to Second Falls and a longer one to Upper Falls. The lot overflows on fall weekends; arrive early or late.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 418.8, Canton, NC 28716

properties.name: Devil's Courthouse
properties.notes: A short, steep paved trail to a rock summit where you can see into four states on a clear day. Peregrine falcons nest on the cliffs, so parts may close in spring.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 422.4, Brevard, NC 28712

properties.name: Richland Balsam Overlook
properties.notes: The highest point on the whole parkway, just over 6,000 feet. The self-guiding trail from the Haywood-Jackson Overlook just north loops through spruce-fir forest that feels more like New England than North Carolina.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 431.4, Sylva, NC 28779

properties.name: Waterrock Knob Visitor Center
properties.notes: A small visitor center with one of the widest views on the road, looking toward the Great Smoky Mountains. A short, steep trail climbs to the summit.
properties.address: Blue Ridge Pkwy, Milepost 451.2, Waynesville, NC 28786

properties.name: Oconaluftee Visitor Center
properties.notes: Just past the parkway's end at milepost 469, the Great Smoky Mountains entrance. Next door the Mountain Farm Museum gathers log farm buildings, and elk often graze the fields at dawn and dusk.
properties.address: 1194 Newfound Gap Rd, Cherokee, NC 28719

properties.name: Museum of the Cherokee People
properties.notes: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians' museum, telling the tribe's history in its own voice, from early life in these mountains through removal and the present. Formerly the Museum of the Cherokee Indian.
properties.address: 589 Tsali Blvd, Cherokee, NC 28719

properties.name: Native Brews Tap & Grill
properties.notes: A Native-owned grill on the main road through Cherokee, with burgers, trout and beer on tap. A relaxed dinner at the end of the road.
properties.address: 1897 Tsali Blvd, Cherokee, NC 28719
